messages:
maria_cs: FYI — Acme reported their month-end invoice is $1.6k higher than the dashboard. They say line items show an extra 'overage buffer' charge that doesn't appear on the dashboard. Can billing team take a look?

sam_billing: Thanks, Maria. Can you paste the invoice lines and dashboard totals? Exact invoice id or customer id helps.

maria_cs: Customer ID: ACME-778. Invoice 2024-03-31 INV-ACME-778-0324. Dashboard shows total $18,240. Invoice shows $19,840. Line items: base plan $10k, usage tokens $8,240, "overage buffer" $1,600.

dina_finance: I pulled the invoice PDF. The buffer line is coming from the 'protection_credit_adjustment' code. Haven't seen that for ACME before.

leo_engineer: Looping in metering-bot for token count diffs. @metering-bot can you run a reconciliation for ACME-778 for 2024-03?

metering-bot: Reconciliation started for ACME-778 (2024-03). Scanning logs, ingest, and aggregation. Will post summary. :gear:

metering-bot: Found mismatch: raw per-request token sum = 8,239,742 tokens. Aggregation pipeline reported 8,240,000 tokens (rounded up to nearest 1,000 for billing). Dashboard shows 8,239,742. Billing pipeline applied thousand-rounding + protection buffer rule resulting in +1,600 USD.

sam_billing: Aha. Our billing pipeline runs "bucket_rounding" that rounds token counts per-customer-per-day to the nearest 1k before applying tiers. Dashboard shows exact token sum. That rounding can move a customer into a higher tier for a day, which triggers the protection buffer if we have burst-smoothing enabled.

maria_cs: So dashboard and invoice disagree because dashboard uses raw tokens and billing uses rounded daily buckets? Customer is asking why they'd pay for tokens that the dashboard doesn't show.

dina_finance: Can we compute how many rounding events happened? If several days rounded up by a few hundred each, that explains the $1.6k.

leo_engineer: Running quick query: 
```
SELECT day, raw_tokens, rounded_tokens FROM billing.daily_buckets
WHERE customer_id='ACME-778' AND month='2024-03';
```
Results: 6 days where rounding up added 258-412 tokens each, total rounded delta = 18,000 tokens. At $0.088/token (example), that is ~$1,584 which matches invoice gap.

sam_billing: That matches. Root cause: billing pipeline policy "round-to-1k-per-day" + protection_policy that adds a 10% buffer fee on days with rounding above threshold. This combo wasn't flagged in the reconciliation checks.

maria_cs: Customer unhappy — they want either invoice adjustment or an explanation + config change. Any quick mitigation?

dina_finance: For this month we can issue a credit equal to the rounding delta and remove the protection buffer charge as a one-off. Need approval from legal? probably not for small amount, finance can approve.

leo_engineer: Tech fix: change billing aggregation to aggregate raw tokens across month before applying rounding/tiering OR switch to rounding at month-level instead of per-day. I'll create a PR to change pipeline and add a unit test. ETA: 1 sprint.

sam_billing: Short-term: mark ACME-778 as "rounding-exempt for 2024-03" so future reruns use raw tokens. I'll file support-credit and refund workflow.

maria_cs: I'll communicate to the customer: apologize, explain the cause (daily rounding in billing pipeline instead of monthly aggregation) and that finance will apply a credit and we will fix the aggregation. Will keep them updated.

dina_finance: I'll draft the credit memo and confirm amount $1,584.00.

leo_engineer: Follow-ups: 1) PR to change rounding rule, 2) Add automated reconciliation check that compares dashboard vs billing monthly sums and flags >0.5% delta, 3) Run a retro on protective buffer config. Assigning to eng/infra and billing teams.

maria_cs: Thanks all. I'll send the customer update now and attach the invoice credit once done. :white_check_mark:
